# One To Many Relation

## Background
A one-to-many relation in Prisma links a parent model to multiple children via a foreign key. This task requires extending the schema with a `Post` model, migrating, and querying users with their posts using `include`.

## Requirements
Add a `Post` model related to `User`, migrate, create a user with posts, then query the user with their posts included.

## Implementation Guide
1. Open `prisma/schema.prisma` and add:
   - A `Post` model: `id Int @id @default(REDACTEDincrement())`, `title String`, `authorId Int`, `author User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])`
   - Add `posts Post[]` back-relation to the `User` model
2. Run: `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_post`
3. Create `/home/user/myproject/relation.js`:
   - Create a user `{ email: 'author@example.com', name: 'Author' }` with two posts nested using `create: { posts: { create: [{ title: 'Post One' }, { title: 'Post Two' }] } }`
   - Query the user with `include: { posts: true }`
   - Write the result to `/home/user/myproject/relation_result.json`
4. Run: `node relation.js`

## Constraints
- Project path: `/home/user/myproject`
- Output file: `/home/user/myproject/relation_result.json`

input.result:
Completed the one-to-many relation task in Prisma.

## What was done

### 1. Schema update (`prisma/schema.prisma`)
Added a `Post` model and the `posts` back-relation on `User`:
```prisma
model User {
  id    Int     @id @default(REDACTEDincrement())
  email String  @unique
  name  String?
  posts Post[]
}

model Post {
  id       Int  @id @default(REDACTEDincrement())
  title    String
  authorId Int
  author   User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
}
```

### 2. Migration
Ran `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_post`, which created and applied migration `20260703054215_add_post` and regenerated the Prisma Client.

### 3. Script (`relation.js`)
Created the script which:
- Cleans existing data (idempotent re-runs)
- Creates a user `author@example.com` / `Author` with two nested posts (`Post One`, `Post Two`) via `create: { posts: { create: [...] } }`
- Queries the user with `include: { posts: true }`
- Writes the result to `relation_result.json`

### 4. Execution
Ran `node relation.js` successfully. The output file `relation_result.json` contains:
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "email": "author@example.com",
  "name": "Author",
  "posts": [
    { "id": 1, "title": "Post One", "authorId": 1 },
    { "id": 2, "title": "Post Two", "authorId": 1 }
  ]
}
```

The one-to-many relation between `User` and `Post` is working, with the user correctly returned alongside both of their posts.
